metadata.model: glm-5.3 (Z.ai GLM), labeled in-session via Claude Code CLI; 4 batches (source batch S1: CSV rows 1-15, source batch S2: rows 16-29, sink batch K1: rows 1-22, sink batch K2: rows 23-44); single labeling pass, no re-ask needed (no entry below the 0.55 confidence threshold); temperature unset (harness default)
notes: Scope: Pass 3 only (CWE-918/099/610, CWE-918 primary); the Pass 1 block is an empty placeholder required by the schema 'contains pass_id 1' constraint (same convention as the earlier django / calibre-web / core / label-studio / fides SSRF runs).
All 29 sources.csv rows and all 44 sinks.csv rows are labeled (73 entries, full row parity); every CSV location is unique, so no deduplication or exclusion was applied.

classification 'tp' asserts only that the labeled role is genuinely played by the API for pass 3 (e.g. requests.request at alignviewers/views.py:42 really fetches the client-supplied remote_url); it never denotes a confirmed vulnerability and no end-to-end SSRF verdict is claimed at this stage.

Primary CWE-918-shaped flows: (1) alignviewers remote_cors arbitrary-URL proxy - /remote/cors/<path:remote_url> forwards the full client URL to requests.request with allow_redirects=True, no scheme/host validation, forwarding inbound headers/body/cookies, reachable by any authenticated user with no institute/case binding; (2) Host-header-derived chanjo coverage POST - request.url_root (cases/views.py:225) -> requests.post(base_url + 'reports/report') (cases/controllers.py:94).

Secondary candidate flow: url_for('report.json_chrom_coverage', _external=True) (cases/controllers.py:544) -> requests.post at :548/:554 - the external URL host derives from the request Host header when SERVER_NAME is unset (scout default); requires the optional SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI chanjo integration. Kept candidate pending deployment-config verification.

No sanitizer entries: no scheme allowlist, host whitelist, redirect control, DNS-resolution or private-IP blocking exists on any audited outbound path; the only scheme check found (url.startswith('ftp') in fetch_resource) is a transport dispatch, not a barrier, and login/role checks (beacon_submitter, institute_and_case) do not constrain outbound URLs.

No summary entries: both tp flows propagate by direct parameter passing and standard interprocedural taint steps (route param -> requests.request url kwarg; request.url_root -> function param -> string concat -> requests.post arg 0); no wrapper-return modeling is needed for Phase 2.

Schema normalizations recorded in labels_raw_pass3.json deviations: url-keyword call sites recorded by the CSV with argIndex -1 normalized to their positional URL index (requests.request url kw -> 1; scout_requests wrapper url kw -> 0); query_phenomizer.query flow_kind 'argument'/argIndex -1 -> flow_kind 'unknown'/arg_index null; sources.csv callableName 'flask.url_for_external' normalized to 'flask.url_for' (no such attribute exists in flask; the site is url_for(..., _external=True)); source argIndex -1 -> arg_index null for non-argument flow kinds.

query_phenomizer.query (cases/controllers.py:837) kept as sink/unknown for human review: its HTTP request happens inside the external query-phenomizer package that is not part of this CodeQL database, so URL-level control cannot be proven or disproven from this source tree.

file: and data: outbound schemes were searched for and not found in scout/ (detection.json coverage_gaps); the only cross-protocol outbound fetch is the ftp branch of fetch_resource (urlopen at scout_requests.py:141), which receives constant ftp URLs only. Local-file concerns (remote_static) are path-traversal territory and were deliberately kept out of CWE-918 labels.
Vulnerability ground truth, fix commits and external CVE descriptions were not consulted; labeling is based only on the scout source tree, the extraction CSVs and exploration/detection.json.

entries.rationale: The <path:remote_url> route converter captures an arbitrary client-supplied URL and the handler forwards it verbatim as the url of requests.request in the same function. There is no scheme validation, no host allowlist and allow_redirects=True; the endpoint requires only an authenticated session (global before_request) with no institute/case binding and no role requirement, so any logged-in user controls the full outbound target. Genuine CWE-918 source boundary.
evidence: scout/server/app.py:83-98 check_user before_request: login is the only gate on this endpoint
scout/server/app.py:54 CORS(app) global - browser origins can call the proxy cross-site

entries.rationale: Inbound headers (minus Host) are forwarded verbatim into the proxied request's headers= argument - not into the URL. They do not control the outbound destination, so they are not a CWE-918 URL source; they are an impact amplifier of the remote_url flow (see src-025) and borderline for header-injection (pass 10), documented here but not labeled for pass 3.
evidence: scout/server/blueprints/alignviewers/views.py:45 headers={key: value for (key, value) in request.headers if key != 'Host'}
URL argument of the same call is remote_url (src-025), not any header value

entries.rationale: request.get_data() is forwarded as the data= (body) argument of the proxied request. Body forwarding never controls the outbound URL; not a CWE-918 source. Companion of the remote_url flow only.

Inbound cookies are forwarded to the attacker-chosen remote target (cookies=request.cookies), which materially amplifies the remote_url SSRF (session-credential exposure). However the cookies never control the destination URL, so for pass 3 URL-forgery labeling they are not a source; recorded as an impact note on the src-025 flow.
evidence: destination control lives exclusively in remote_url (src-025)

entries.rationale: The remote CORS proxy transport: requests.request(method=request.method, url=remote_url, headers=..., data=..., cookies=..., allow_redirects=True) where remote_url is the full client-supplied route path variable (src-025). No scheme/host validation, redirects followed, inbound headers/body/cookies forwarded. The URL argument position is the url= keyword, i.e. positional argument 1 of requests.request (CSV argIndex -1 normalized to 1). Sink role genuinely played: the outbound target is fully attacker-chosen by any authenticated user.
